claim: Readers infer a writer's attitude from an essay even when told the position was assigned (correspondence bias); the effect persists under coercion in modern samples.
agent_test: Give the agent vignettes with assigned vs free-choice positions; measure attitude inference gap, with and without a 'was this chosen?' check step, at equal tokens.
audit_note: Gill 2014 Study 5 verified (no-choice d=.84, t(84)=3.83; choice d=2.0); Kirkland preprint abstract confirms N=1,611 and assigned-position paradigm; Gill and Kirkland share author Bastian, so modern-sample support is less independent than it looks.

claim: Correspondence bias is large in US samples: coerced-essay position effects d about 0.84 to 1.6, and explicit debiasing instructions only partly reduce it.
agent_test: Same as K01 plus explicit-adjustment prompt arm.
audit_note: Gill d=.84 and Kirkland d=1.58/1.64 are consistent with the range; Moore et al. abstract confirms bias persists under debiasing treatments but the Study 2 table could not be read; 'US samples' not verifiable from accessible text (Gill Study 5 country not stated); Gill and Kirkland share author Bastian.

claim: East Asians (Koreans, Japanese) show weaker correspondence bias when the situational constraint is salient or the attitude has low diagnosticity; Americans do not adjust. Gap search: in Norenzayan et al. (manuscript) Koreans (N=100) equal Americans (N=97) on dispositionism and exceed them on situationism (5.91 vs 5.43, F(1,191)=4.44); the salience effect rests on N=58, interaction p near .05.
agent_test: Prompt with salient constraint and in Korean/English; compare inference shift. Sources are mostly secondary reviews; no cell sizes read.
audit_note: Norenzayan, Choi & Nisbett Study 1 (100 vs 97, 5.91 vs 5.43, F(1,191)=4.44, p<.05) and Study 2 (N=58, 3-way F(1,50)=4.60, p<.05) verified in the PDF; Mason & Morris review text confirms the Choi & Nisbett and Miyamoto & Kitayama findings; note Study 2 measures behaviour prediction not attitude attribution, and the three Nisbett-lab sources are one lab.

claim: Culture priming effect on internal attribution replicates in young Chinese (Hong Kong N=107 d=1.48; Mainland N=272 f2=.195) but not in older Mainland adults (N=258, f2=.009).
agent_test: Test whether a persona or culture prompt shifts LLM attributions as strongly as in young humans.

claim: Spontaneous trait inference is large (dz=0.59, k=86, N=13,630) and culture does not significantly moderate it (p=.239), though single studies found culture differences.
agent_test: Spontaneous inference probe in LLM (trait-word completion) across culture prompts.

claim: The actor-observer asymmetry is near zero in meta-analysis (173 studies, d -0.016 to 0.095) and appears only under specific conditions.
agent_test: Do not hard-code an actor/observer correction; test only if the effect appears in role-swapped LLM prompts.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Cognitive load and salience raise correspondence bias; explicit reflective steps reduce but do not remove it. Hidden reasoning budget did not reduce LLM self-attribution bias (Khullar 2026), so token budget is not a clean analogue of human load.
agent_test: Compare short vs long deliberation arms on FAE vignettes at equal tokens.

claim: Heavy debiasing reduces but leaves the effect intact, and correspondence bias also appears for inanimate objects (+0.208 g per container gram), suggesting a general anchoring-like mechanism.
agent_test: Run the container-weight task on the LLM.

claim: Correspondence bias extends to robots: effect larger for robot behaviour (Beta -0.76) than humans (-0.48) in 231 US adults.
agent_test: Ask the agent to attribute actions of AI agents; compare with humans.

claim: LLMs show small FAE bias on a role-swap (actor vs observer) test: mean 0.10 on a -1 to 1 scale across 20 models, range -0.02 to 0.23, random baseline 0.03; far below information bias (0.54) and in-group bias (0.41). Value now verified in the paper's heatmap.
agent_test: Replicate the test on our agent.

claim: GPT-4 lowers inferred attitude as coercion strength rises (discounts for pressure) in a blog test; no numbers.
agent_test: Replicate with N and numbers across pressure levels.

claim: ChatGPT leans toward Eastern holistic thinking on AHS/TCT but self-construal measures are mixed; temperature and wording did not change this.
agent_test: Do not assume the model is Western-analytic; measure per prompt language.

claim: Prompting for a country raises cultural alignment for 71-81% of countries in the GPT-4 family; weak for GPT-3/3.5. Gap search: the shift is in survey-value distance (GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57), not in attribution; no LLM culture-prompt vs human-priming comparison exists.
agent_test: Use culture prompts only as a probe, not as an agent guard.

claim: LLMs shift ability/effort vs luck/difficulty attributions by identity cues, but direction differs by model: Aya-8B favours external causes for success and failure, Qwen-32B and Llama-70B lean internal (effort). Earlier wording 'failure is internalised in all three models' was not supported.
agent_test: Swap identity in outcome-attribution prompts; measure shift at equal tokens.

claim: A prior psychiatric label raises LLM recommendations of continued hospitalisation from 4.7% to 22.3% (risk difference 17.5 pts, 5 models): a dispositional-label bias.
agent_test: Label-swap probe with and without a 'check evidence only' step.

claim: LLMs have a self-correction blind spot (64.5% mean across 14 models) cut 89.3% by a 'Wait' prompt. It is an authorship effect: the same error is fixed when labelled the user's and missed when labelled the model's; on natural errors only 4.3-10.8% are caught when shown externally.
agent_test: Add a Wait step to the scaffold; measure at equal tokens.

claim: Multi-agent failure attribution is hard: best step-level accuracy 14.2% with 53.5% agent-level; hybrid all-at-once then step-by-step gives 57.02% agent / 12.28% step at 8.7x the tokens of all-at-once (4.39% step); o1 and R1 do not reliably beat GPT-4o. Intervention-based checks (DoVer) help but have no equal-token comparison.
agent_test: Test whether scaffold traces can be blamed accurately; use intervention checks (DoVer-style).
audit_note: Who&When abstract (53.5%/14.2%) and Table 3 (hybrid 57.02/12.28 at 149,177 vs 17,106 tokens = 8.7x; all-at-once 4.39) and Table 4 verified; DoVer abstract confirms intervention approach but the 'no equal-token comparison' remark is an absence claim not checkable.

claim: Implicit-causality bias in GPT-2 is weak (only 32% of continuations rated >=4).
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: A single preprint (N=1,611 across three studies) found mixed evidence in Studies 1-2 and, in preregistered Study 3, that stronger moral conviction predicted more dispositional inference, mainly when participants agreed with the essay; the underlying correspondence-bias effect of essay position was large (d up to 1.64) regardless.
agent_test: Probe LLM with morally charged assigned essays.
audit_note: Kirkland abstract says Studies 1-2 were mixed and only preregistered Study 3 found moral conviction predicting more dispositional inference (mainly when participants agreed with the essay); d up to 1.64 is the essay-position effect itself, not the conviction effect; Gill is not about moral conviction so there is a single preprint source.
claim_before_audit: Moral conviction amplifies correspondence bias (N=1,611; d up to 1.64).

claim: Causal role assignment in symmetric events varies by culture (Germany vs Tonga) in concrete settings but not covariation settings.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: The claim that Hindu children give more situational explanations rests on a web explainer, not a study.
agent_test: Do not cite.

claim: LLMs judge the same action as more correct and less risky when it is implicitly their own (previous assistant turn): code-correctness AUROC 0.99 off-policy vs 0.89 on-policy same-turn (Claude Sonnet 4 monitor). Explicit 'same model' wording alone does not cause it; more reasoning tokens does not reliably fix it.
agent_test: Run the scaffold's self-check in the same turn vs a fresh user turn at equal tokens; compare detection AUROC on known-bad outputs.

claim: Authorship framing changes self-correction: the same injected error is corrected when user-attributed and missed when model-attributed (64.5% blind spot, 14 models); appending Wait cuts it 89.3%.
agent_test: Wait arm vs no-Wait on label-swap and identity probes (untested for attribution bias).

claim: Koreans match Americans on disposition use and differ on situation weight: N=100 vs 97 dispositionism 5.19 vs 5.00 (F<1), situationism 5.91 vs 5.43 (p<.05); replicated with N=120 vs 121 (4.82 vs 4.59 ns; situationism 5.27 vs 4.67, F(1,240)=8.47). Manuscript version, no effect sizes.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: No LLM Jones-Harris study with numbers and no large preregistered cross-cultural replication of the East-West correspondence-bias difference was found, but the search was blocked by rate limits and is incomplete.
agent_test: Run our own assigned-vs-chosen essay test with graded pressure.

claim: Fault attribution by LLMs depends on disputant gender with conduct fixed: male agents +0.16 on a 0-7 scale (dz=0.316, 1,458 vignettes, 5 LLMs); varies by model and norm family.
agent_test: Swap identity labels in blame vignettes and compare ratings.
